facts.raw_span: a 3-year history of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions
Previous treatments with various topical glucocorticosteroids and antibiotics showed no improvement
occasional otitis media
The family history was negative for skin disease
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules, petechial hemorrhages, and yellowish crusts were present on the scalp
Neck, axillary, and inguinal lymph nodes showed no abnormalities
Routine blood examinations revealed no pathological findings

Subepidermal infiltrate consisting of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei, solitary lymphocytes, and eosinophilic granulocytes
The infiltrate stained positively for CD1A
Ultrasonography of abdomen and lymph nodes: normal
Serum electrophoresis: normal
